claims.text: The default ListView constructor takes a children list whose widgets are all created before the ListView exists, so creating them costs work in proportion to the number of items.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: cookbook/lists/long-lists.md ('the default ListView constructor, which requires creating all items at once'); api.flutter.dev ListView constructor

claims.text: ListView.builder takes itemCount and itemBuilder (BuildContext, int index) and, while laying out, calls itemBuilder only for indexes in or near the visible area, more as the user scrolls; itemCount alone creates no widget.
claims.source_hint: api.flutter.dev ListView.builder ('called only for those children that are actually visible'); refs/flutter-website: cookbook/lists/long-lists.md; perf/best-practices.md ('Be lazy!')

claims.text: With ListView.builder, rows that scroll well past the edge of the visible area are removed (when they do not ask to be kept alive, as ProductTile does not), and itemBuilder is called again for them when they scroll back.
claims.source_hint: api.flutter.dev ListView ('Child elements' lifecycle' section); SliverChildBuilderDelegate addAutomaticKeepAlives; probe run at stage-3

claims.text: GridView.builder builds its children on demand in the same way as ListView.builder, with itemCount and itemBuilder.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: ui/layout/scrolling/index.md ('build the items on demand as they scroll into view ... ListView.builder or GridView.builder'); api.flutter.dev GridView.builder

claims.text: Stage-3 ProductCatalog.build: LayoutBuilder; below wideLayoutMinWidth (600) ListView.builder, else GridView.builder, gridDelegate crossAxisCount = floor(maxWidth / columnWidth), mainAxisExtent Sizes.gridRow; both pass itemCount: products.length and an itemBuilder calling _tile.

Stage-3 test 'a long list builds only the tiles near the screen': 10 000 products, catalog in SizedBox 360x400, expects one 'Product 1' text, no 'Product 10000' text, fewer than 30 ProductTile widgets.

At stage-3, flutter test test/product_catalog_test.dart passes ('All tests passed!'); changing find.text('Product 1') to find.text('Product 100') in the long-list test makes it fail on that expect, since no widget shows 'Product 100'.
claims.source_hint: run flutter test in DonHang.App at stage-3 (Flutter 3.47); not run during generation

claims.text: find.text and find.byType skip offstage widgets by default (skipOffstage: true); rows of a scrolling list outside the visible area count as offstage, so the stage-3 test's three expects look only at what is on screen, and the on-screen count depends on box and tile height.
claims.source_hint: api.flutter.dev CommonFinders.text / byType (skipOffstage); refs/flutter-website release-notes-0.0.21-1.0.0.md ('children of a viewport that are currently not visible ... off-stage')

claims.text: List length alone is no reason to page when a builder list is used; paging is worth it when fetching or holding the whole list costs too much, decided by the data (how much travels, how long a request takes).
claims.source_hint: outline items 3 and 5; refs/flutter-website: ui/layout/scrolling/index.md (builder lists for long or infinite lists)
